app_shell.s:
Build the frame everything else slots into: src/routes/+layout.ts, src/routes/+layout.svelte, src/routes/+page.svelte. src/routes/+layout.ts (new file): ```ts export const ssr = false; export const prerender = true; ``` Why: sinc is 100% client-side — files never leave the browser, there is no server work to do. Prerendering the shell makes the Cloudflare deploy pure static assets (no Worker invocation, no cost), and ssr=false stops Kit trying to render components that touch document/AudioContext at build time. src/routes/+layout.svelte — keep whatever the scaffold generated (it imports ./layout.css and renders {@render children()}), but make its wrapper fill the viewport: ```svelte
{@render children()}
``` src/routes/+page.svelte — the four-region chassis. Placeholders now; later steps replace each region's inner markup, never this grid. ```svelte
sinc {p.w}×{p.h} · {p.f}fps
{tc(ui.pf, p.f)}
library
``` Region contract for later steps — do not rename these: - data-r="topbar": name, size/fps, timecode, import / render / settings buttons - data-r="library": sources list + clip grid - data-r="stage": row 1 is the viewport canvas (or the clip-maker when ui.mode === 'c'), row 2 is the transport - data-r="timeline": ruler + marker rail + track rows gap-px on a bg-line parent is how every seam in sinc is drawn — one shared hairline system, no border utilities scattered around. TESTS — src/routes/page.svelte.spec.ts (client project), written first: ```ts import { render } from 'vitest-browser-svelte'; import { expect, test } from 'vitest'; import Page from './+page.svelte'; test('shell has all four regions', async () => { const s = render(Page); for (const r of ['topbar', 'library', 'stage', 'timeline']) await expect.element(s.baseElement.querySelector(`[data-r="${r}"]`)!).toBeInTheDocument(); }); ``` Also confirm `pnpm run build` succeeds (it must prerender / to a static file). Then `pnpm run check`, `pnpm run lint`. Commit as "app shell".

polish_and_ship.s:
Final pass on the v1 app, then deploy.

1. Empty states. With no sources: the library shows a dashed drop zone reading "drop video, audio or images" and the stage shows the three-line quickstart in text-dim font-mono — "import media · press b on the beat · press c to cut". No blank panels anywhere.

2. Key chips. Every button that has a keyboard equivalent renders its key in a `<kbd>` styled `bg-panel2 text-dim font-mono text-[10px] px-1 rounded`. This is how the keyboard workflow gets discovered without a manual.

3. Accessibility floor (do not trade this away): every icon-only button gets aria-label; the marker rail buttons already have one; :focus-visible is already styled globally; timeline items are `<button>` elements so they are tabbable; the render dialog is a real `<dialog>` with showModal() so focus is trapped for free.

4. Responsive floor: below 900px wide, stack the library UNDER the stage (grid-cols-1) and drop the timeline to h-56. sinc is a desktop tool and that is fine — but it must not be visually broken on a laptop in a split screen.

5. Kill-test pass against the concept sentence from step design_tokens. Check honestly: does the marker rail actually flash on the beat during playback? Is there exactly ONE accent colour doing work? Is every number font-mono and tabular? If any panel has crept into a second accent hue, remove it.

6. README.md — replace the scaffold text with: what sinc is (one paragraph), the full keymap table, the "everything stays in your browser" note, and the browser requirement (WebCodecs: Chrome/Edge/Safari 17+; Firefox works if it can encode, otherwise the render step throws a clear message).

7. Ship:
   - `pnpm run lint && pnpm run check && pnpm run test:unit -- --run && pnpm run build` — all four green.
   - `gh repo create angelwingscomms/sinc --public --source=. --remote=origin --push`
   - `pnpm dlx wrangler deploy` (wrangler.jsonc already names the worker "sinc" and points at .svelte-kit/cloudflare). Confirm the deployed URL loads and an import → mark → cut → render round-trip works in the browser.

TESTS: no new unit tests. The gate for this step is all four commands green plus a manual round-trip on the deployed URL. Commit as "polish + ship v1", then push.

ms_service.s:
PHASE 2 — automatic beat/note detection. Nothing before this step depends on it; v1 must already be shipped and green.

Background (verified 2026-07-30): the library the user means is MuScriptor, open-sourced by Mirelo AI (mirelo.ai) with Kyutai. It is a decoder-only transformer that takes a mel-spectrogram of a 5-second audio chunk and autoregressively emits tokens encoding pitch, timing and instrument — i.e. multi-instrument audio→MIDI on a full mix, with automatic instrument labelling plus chord/key/tempo detection. Python, MIT licence. Weights: huggingface.co/MuScriptor/muscriptor-medium (and -large). Inference code: github.com/muscriptor/muscriptor.

Why this is NOT in the SvelteKit app: it is a PyTorch transformer needing a GPU. It cannot run in a Cloudflare Worker, and porting the weights to ONNX/transformers.js for in-browser inference is its own multi-week project, not a step. Ship it as a tiny separate service.
// ponytail: separate Python service on serverless GPU. Revisit in-browser ONNX only if someone actually needs offline transcription.

Work:
1. `git clone https://github.com/muscriptor/muscriptor ~/i/muscriptor` and READ its README before writing any code — the exact inference entrypoint, input sample rate, and output schema must come from the repo, not from this step. Everything below is the shape to fill in, not a guess to copy blindly.
2. Create ~/i/sinc/svc/transcribe.py, a Modal app (serverless GPU, scales to zero, so an idle sinc costs nothing):
```python
import modal

image = (
    modal.Image.debian_slim()
    .apt_install("ffmpeg")
    .pip_install("torch", "torchaudio", "transformers", "huggingface_hub", "fastapi[standard]")
)
app = modal.App("sinc-transcribe", image=image)


@app.function(gpu="A10G", timeout=600, scaledown_window=120)
@modal.fastapi_endpoint(method="POST")
def transcribe(audio: bytes):
    # 1. decode the audio bytes to mono float32 at the model's sample rate (torchaudio)
    # 2. run muscriptor inference -> note events
    # 3. collapse to onsets per instrument
    return {
        "t": [  # one entry per detected instrument
            {"n": "kick", "o": [0.501, 0.998, 1.502]},  # onsets, SECONDS
        ]
    }
```
Keep the response schema exactly `{ t: [{ n: string, o: number[] }] }` — single-letter keys, onsets in seconds (the client converts to frames, because only the client knows the project fps).
3. `pip install modal && modal setup && modal deploy svc/transcribe.py`. Put the resulting URL in .env as `MS_URL` (NEVER .dev.vars) and read it client-side via a `PUBLIC_MS_URL` var — this endpoint is called from the browser, so it must be public; add Modal's proxy-auth token if you want it gated.
4. Add svc/README.md: deploy command, cost note, and the fact that audio bytes leave the browser for this feature ONLY (v1 is fully local — say so plainly, it is a real privacy change).

TESTS: svc/test_transcribe.py — a pytest that posts a 3-second click track generated with numpy (a 1kHz burst every 0.5s, written to wav) to the deployed endpoint and asserts the response has at least one instrument whose onsets are within ±60ms of [0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5]. Run it against the real deployment; a mocked test proves nothing here. Commit as "muscriptor service".
